source_text: Nam ut duri cordis tunc et impiae plebis ad Domini metum ipso Domino euangelizante conuersas mentes sileam, ut apostolorum eius praedicatione multiplicatum in orbe toto et refersum credentium populum conticiscam: illud praeclarum atque memorabile gloriosumque Iasonis Hebraei Christiani et Papisci Alexandrini Iudaei disceptationis occurrit, Iudaici cordis obstinatam duritiam Hebraei admonitione ac leni increpatione mollitam, uictricem in Papisci corde Iasonis de spiritus sancti infusione doctrinam, qua Papiscus ad intellectum ueritatis admissus et ad timorem Domini ipso Domino miserante formatus et legum Christum Dei filium credidit et ut signaculum sumeret deprecatus Iasonem postulauit. probat hoc scriptura concertationis ipsorum, quae collidentium inter se Papisci aduersantis ueritati et Iasonis adserentis et uindicantis dispositionem et plenitudinem Christi Graeci sermonis opere signata est: ad cuius translationem in intellectum Latinum animante Domini ope et uiuentis fidei firmitate seruata uerborum proprietate intrepidus accessi: et his qui ab intellectu Graecae docilitatis alieni sunt interpretata integra significatione uerborum et intellectus omnis ac ueritatis manifestatione patefacta Romani sermonis ratione discussa disserui. cuius laboris probationem tibi, carissime, qui utriusque linguae instructione fundatus es, impensa petitione committo: ut qui sancti spiritus ueneratione uerecundus es conlata utriusque operis lectione audaciam uerecundae temeritatis explores et examine iudicii tui quae minus a nobis uel improprie forte digesta sunt auctoritate spiritus sancti, qui in pectus tuum inundatione gratiae caelestis influxit, comprobes et emendes: sitque ad te de ista lectione ab humilitate nostra mandata legatio et insinuanda tibi in nos prima dilectionis petitio, ut paruitatem fidei meae cum discipulorum tuorum instructione atque eruditione coniungas et me, quem in alia parte huius prouinciae constitutum propter uisendos uultus tuos non itineris longinquitas terruit nec senium ac difficultas fatigati ac fessi iam corporis redarguit, sed animante stimulatu Domini et urgente festinato cupiditate properandi, contempta quoque omni tribulatione inopiae atque penuriae quantacumque uirium facultate ueniendi, sanctimoniae tuae celebris huc fama perduxit, ad promixtum dilectus tui caritate cum unanimitate fraternitatis admittas et amori tuo quem discipulis suis Dominus hereditatis titulo reliquit coniungas pariter et adsciscas, exspectem cum fratribus pariter in apertione oris tui splendorem gratiae luminis Christi, sequar in tractatibus tuis lumen quod Dominus ostendit, quod Christus adueniens aeternam uitam esse monstrauit.
thought_title: The memorable dispute of Jason and Papiscus and the author's translation
orientation: The author is addressing Vigilius, explaining that he will pass over the conversion of the hardened Jewish people under the Lord's own preaching and the apostles' spread of believers, and instead present the famous dispute between Jason and Papiscus, whose translation he has made and now submits to Vigilius for review.
pass_a_gloss: For that I may be silent about the converted minds of the then hard-hearted and impious people at the fear of the Lord, with the Lord himself preaching the gospel, that I may keep quiet about the multiplied and filled-up people of believers in the whole world by the preaching of his apostles: that famous and memorable and glorious dispute of Jason the Hebrew Christian and Papiscus the Alexandrian Jew comes to mind, the obstinate hardness of the Jewish heart softened by the admonition and gentle rebuke of the Hebrew, the victorious teaching of Jason in the heart of Papiscus from the infusion of the Holy Spirit, by which teaching Papiscus, admitted to the understanding of the truth and formed to the fear of the Lord with the Lord himself showing mercy, both believed Christ to be the Son of God and asked Jason, entreating him, that he might receive the seal. This the writing of their dispute proves, which has been marked in a work of Greek speech of the colliding with each other of Papiscus opposing the truth and of Jason asserting and defending the arrangement and fullness of Christ: to the translation of which into Latin understanding, with the Lord's help giving courage and with the firmness of living faith preserved and the propriety of the words kept, I came without fear: and for those who are strangers to the understanding of Greek learning, with the whole meaning of the words interpreted and the manifestation of every understanding and truth laid open, I set it forth, having examined the method of Roman speech. The testing of which labor I commit to you, dearest one, who have been founded in the instruction of both languages, with earnest entreaty: so that you, who are reverent in the veneration of the Holy Spirit, may examine the boldness of my reverent rashness by comparing the reading of both works, and by the judgment of your examination may approve and correct what has perhaps been set down by us less well or improperly, by the authority of the Holy Spirit, who has flowed into your breast by an inundation of heavenly grace: and may there be to you from our humility an embassy entrusted concerning this reading, and a first petition of love to be made known to you in us, that you may join the smallness of my faith with the instruction and training of your disciples, and that you may admit me, whom, established in another part of this province, not the length of the journey terrified for the sake of seeing your face, nor did old age and the difficulty of a tired and worn-out body refute, but the encouraging goad of the Lord and the urgent hastened desire of hurrying, with every tribulation of want and poverty also despised, with whatever ability of strength there was for coming, the celebrated fame of your holiness brought here, to the nearness of your beloved by love with the unanimity of brotherhood, and may you join and also take me up to your love, which the Lord left to his disciples by the title of inheritance, may I await with the brothers equally in the opening of your mouth the splendor of the grace of the light of Christ, may I follow in your treatises the light which the Lord shows, which Christ coming showed to be eternal life.

choices.why: The glossary gives 'hardness of heart' for duritia cordis; here duritia stands alone with Iudaici cordis, so 'hardness' preserves the literal sense.
The glossary mandates 'seal' for signaculum, referring to baptism.
The glossary mandates 'fear' for timor, the reverent fear of God.
The verb credo is rendered 'believed' to keep the literal sense of Papiscus's act of faith.
The adjective uictricem modifies doctrinam and is rendered literally as 'victorious' to preserve the image of Jason's teaching winning in Papiscus's heart.
The author calls his own boldness 'reverent rashness'; 'rashness' keeps the literal self-deprecating force.

pass_b_english: For I will pass over in silence how the minds of that hard-hearted and impious people were turned to the fear of the Lord when the Lord himself preached the gospel to them, and how the people of believers was multiplied and filled throughout the whole world by the preaching of his apostles. What comes to mind instead is that famous, memorable, and glorious dispute between Jason, a Hebrew Christian, and Papiscus, an Alexandrian Jew. The obstinate hardness of the Jewish heart was softened by the Hebrew's admonition and gentle rebuke. Jason's teaching, victorious in Papiscus's heart through the infusion of the Holy Spirit, brought Papiscus to an understanding of the truth. Formed in the fear of the Lord by the Lord's own mercy, he believed that Christ is the Son of God and begged Jason and asked that he receive the seal.

The writing of their contest proves this. It is a work in the Greek language that records the clash between Papiscus, who opposed the truth, and Jason, who asserted and defended the fullness of Christ. I approached the translation of it into Latin understanding without fear, with the Lord's help animating me and the firmness of living faith preserving the propriety of the words. For those who are strangers to the understanding of Greek learning, I have set it forth in Roman speech, with the complete meaning of the words interpreted and every understanding and manifestation of the truth laid open.

I commit the testing of this labor to you, dearest friend, who are grounded in the instruction of both languages, with earnest entreaty. You are reverent in your veneration of the Holy Spirit. By reading both works side by side, examine the boldness of my reverent rashness. By the judgment of your discernment, approve and correct whatever I may have set down poorly or improperly, by the authority of the Holy Spirit who has flowed into your heart with an inundation of heavenly grace.

Let this message be sent to you from my humility about this reading, and let this first request of love be made known to you on my behalf: that you join the smallness of my faith with the instruction and training of your disciples. I am settled in another part of this province. The length of the journey did not frighten me from seeing your face, nor did old age and the difficulty of a tired and weary body hold me back. The goad of the Lord animated me, and an urgent, hastening desire pressed me on. I scorned every tribulation of want and poverty, and came with whatever strength I had. The widespread fame of your holiness led me here. Admit me to your presence, joined with the love of your beloved and the unanimity of the brotherhood. Join me and receive me into that love which the Lord left to his disciples as an inheritance. Let me wait with the brothers for the splendor of the grace of Christ's light in the opening of your mouth. Let me follow in your teachings the light that the Lord has shown, the light that Christ at his coming revealed to be eternal life.

problems.quote: asked Jason, begging him to receive the seal
problems.source_quote: ut signaculum sumeret deprecatus Iasonem postulauit
problems.why: Papiscus begged and asked Jason that he (Papiscus) receive the seal, not Jason.
problems.fix: begged Jason and asked that he receive the seal
problems.ruling: Latin 'ut signaculum sumeret deprecatus Iasonem postulauit' shows Papiscus (subject) begged and asked Jason that he (Papiscus) receive the seal; English reverses agents.

fixed: Corrected: source 'ut signaculum sumeret deprecatus Iasonem postulauit' means Papiscus begged Jason and asked that he (Papiscus) receive the seal, not that Jason receive it.
